scope.description: The frozen 51-case Phase 3F.1.5 stratified sample only (not the full DSGR dataset, which would trigger ~14,238 calls). All generated pairs for these 51 gtUnitIds were deterministically evaluated first; the live judge was consulted only for pairs the deterministic layer marked INDETERMINATE.

callStats.costMethodology: 777,455 input + 220,720 output tokens against Claude Haiku 4.5's published per-token pricing (~$1/MTok in, ~$5/MTok out) - an estimate from public rate cards, not authoritative Vercel AI Gateway billing data. Well within the $15 budget the user authorized (12.5% used); the run never approached the 2,000-call safety cap (592 of 2,000 used) because only 592 of the sample's 3,060 generated pairs were deterministically INDETERMINATE.

inputDisciplineCompliance: buildJudgeUserPrompt (unchanged from ./adjudication.ts) sends only the GT excerpt/semantic description and the candidate's own excerpts/normalized semantics/provenance - never V2's own historical disposition, never the second-pass result, never whether a case is one of the 14 known false credits.

comparisonAgainstDeterministicOnlyBaseli.note: Compares this live-informed run's per-unit matchStatus/representationStatus against the ORIGINAL deterministic-only sealed labels (docs/evaluation-v2/_stratified-sample-v2-labels-SEALED.json, byte-identical, unmodified) for the same 51 gtUnitIds.

changes.creditImplication: No change - both dispositions are NO_CREDIT. The live judge downgraded an active contradiction flag to a plain non-match, a refinement in kind of explanation, not in credit outcome.

No change - both dispositions are NO_CREDIT. The live judge found a candidate that surfaces uncertainty rather than confirming the deterministic layer's 'nothing corresponds' reading - a safer classification, but not a credit change.

comparisonAgainstDeterministicOnlyBaseli.criticalFinding: NEITHER changed unit overlaps with the 32 detailed disagreements (or the 11 binary disagreements) forensically classified in 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json - confirmed by direct set-intersection against that artifact's full case list, which is empty. In other words: on this exact sample, actually running a live semantic judge - the second of Phase 3F.1.5's two hypothesized confounders - changed ZERO of the original disagreement cases' dispositions, and even the 2 unrelated cases it did touch stayed within the same credit outcome (NO_CREDIT). This is a direct, now-tested answer to the open question 13-remaining-evaluation-risks.json flagged: the absence of a live judge does NOT appear to be a material driver of the original second-pass disagreement on this sample. The 'communication gap' hypothesis (the taxonomy-vocabulary mismatch documented in 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json, responsible for 65.6% of detailed disagreements) remains the only confounder with real, demonstrated explanatory power; the live-judge confounder is now tested and does not hold up on this evidence.
